content.text: No liquidated damages or penalty clause payable by Customer exists anywhere in the agreement.

input.quote: Fees do not include taxes, reimbursable expenses, service credits, interest, damages, or a one-time implementation charge unless an Order Form expressly states otherwise.
input.rationale: The agreement contains no liquidated damages, penalty, or early-termination/minimum-fee-on-termination obligation payable by Customer, which matches the preferred position. Searches for "liquidated", "penalt", "remaining", acceleration and make-whole language returned nothing adverse: § 1.5 excludes service credits, interest and damages from Fees; § 7.3 bars interest on amounts ultimately found not due; § 9 (termination) imposes no exit charge on Customer; § 24.4 expressly denies Vendor any right to accelerate Fees; and § 27.3 lets Customer terminate for prolonged force majeure "without penalty." The only Customer payment obligations found are undisputed Fees for conforming Services (§ 7.1, § 21.3) and audit costs plus the actual undisputed shortfall where an audit shows underpayment above five percent (§ 22.2) — both compensatory, not liquidated damages. The take-or-pay commitment in § 2.1 is economically penal in effect, but that commercial term is addressed under the minimum-commitment rule and is not double-flagged here. No redline required.
